title: Protein Functional Semantic Alignment via Representation Rectification
claimed_delta: SAVR vs vanilla PLM backbone, Fmax/AUPR and linear-probe macro-F1 gains
note: no seed, sd, error-bar or repetition language anywhere in the full text; frozen backbone + one-hidden-layer MLP classifier (has a training seed)

title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
claimed_delta: 100M head, mean TM: one-hot 0.346, untrained-Qwen states 0.347, protein-trained Qwen states 0.712, ESM2-3B control 0.375
note: explicit: 'The intervals quantify variation across entries for one trained model per configuration' - bootstrap is over test entries, not over seeds

title: Multi-Assay Antibody Developability Prediction with Shared Structure-Language Representations
benchmarks: in-house antibody developability assays (PK, AC-SINS, SMP, BVP, ...)
claimed_delta: two-stream (physicochemical + PLM) vs single stream; multi-assay training raises Spearman rho ~0.1 on ovalbumin and SMP
note: 5 random seeds averaged per cross-validation fold, 5 cluster-split folds; reports seed-to-seed variance explicitly

title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
note: PLM contact maps are read out without a trained head; the Potts baseline is fitted but the PLM arm has no training seed. The 'three seeds' in the text are alphabet-relabeling seeds, not training seeds - a regex-only pass would have recorded k=3 here.

title: MutAtlas: A PDB-Wide Energy-Guided Atlas of Protein Mutation Effects
note: 'All models are evaluated in a zero-shot manner. No experimental mutation data from ProteinGym are used during training.'

title: HyPLM Technical Report
claimed_delta: HyPLM-Flash vs ESM-2 650M / ESM C 600M / E1-600M across frozen-representation tasks; ProteinGym zero-shot 0.409, 'statistically tied'
note: probes are closed-form ridge and L-BFGS logistic regressions, so most arms are deterministic and have no training seed; the contact head alone is AdamW-trained. NOTABLE: they drop GB1 two-vs-rest, three-vs-rest and the FLIP2 hydrolase split from all summary statistics because 'numerically equivalent runs of the same model differ by up to 0.2' - independent corroboration of the Part B GB1 instability.

title: ProtLink: Sequence and Multispecies Graph Context for Protein Interaction Prediction
claimed_delta: human-only AP 0.9442+-0.0097 vs orthogroup 0.9526+-0.0042 (paired +0.0084); full multispecies 0.9701+-0.0022 (paired +0.0266, positive in all three seeds)
note: reports per-seed AP and mean+-SD and explicitly declines to infer significance from three repetitions; also reports paired per-seed deltas and compares the gain against cross-seed variation - the practice this project argues for

title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
claimed_delta: GLP vs InterPLM SAE features, ESM feedforward neurons and raw residual stream, at ESM-2-8M and ESM-2-650M; discrete AUC and continuous Spearman rho
note: 1-D logistic probes with inner 5-fold CV, so the probe fit is near-deterministic, but the GLP arm comes from a trained diffusion model whose seed count is never stated. The 'three runs' in the text are independent steering experiments, not probe seeds.

title: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
note: ProtT5 and MolT5 stay frozen in every arm; the ablation varies the readout and pooling, never the representation. No PLM-vs-non-PLM or PLM-vs-PLM comparison. (It does use 10 folds x 3 seeds, which a regex pass would have credited to a representation comparison that does not exist.)

title: When Can You Trust Neural Critics? Auditing Mutual Information Estimates of Higher-Order Epistasis in Protein Language Models
note: Arms are MI estimators, evaluation pairings and ESM-2 layers, not representations against a baseline representation. RELATED WORK, cite: it measures cross-seed SD of trained critics on GB1 and shows run-to-run differences are 'comparable to ordinary cross-seed retraining variability' - the same argument as this project, for MI estimation rather than representation gains.

title: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes
benchmarks: in-house ordered/disordered ensemble benchmark (RMSE, SAXS, Flory exponent)
claimed_delta: ESM2-650M replaced by ESM2-8M, plus pair-representation, alignment and training-source ablations; seed-averaged log RMSE differences, negligible if within +-5%
note: entered under Amendment 3. Among the most careful in the pool: per-seed training, paired seed-averaged deltas, bootstrap SE over proteins, a pre-stated negligibility band, and an explicit limitation that three seeds leave small cells unresolved

title: TACFormer: Transformer-Based Generative Model for Target-Conditioned De Novo PROTAC Design
note: Protein conditioning is present but never compared against an alternative protein representation; the contrast is conditional vs unconditional generation. Three seeds x 200k molecules, but for generation metrics, not a representation comparison.

title: Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap: Persistent Homology Enables Cross-Species Ion Channel Classification via Multimodal Graph Neural Networks
benchmarks: in-house venom ion-channel set, random split and leave-one-taxon-out
claimed_delta: ESM+GAT baseline vs PH-GNN and five other geometric priors; accuracy and macro F1, in-distribution and leave-one-taxon-out
note: explicit and disclosed: 'Reported results reflect a single training run per model. Data splits are deterministically seeded (random_state=42); however, network initializations are unseeded.' Variance is quantified by McNemar and bootstrap over a FIXED test set - test-item variance presented as if it covered run variance, which is precisely the conflation this project measures.

title: recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models
claimed_delta: recAMPLIFY vs ESM-2 150M and 650M; improves three of four supervised probes
note: best HPO configuration retrained with 5 random seeds; mean in the main table, SD in Appendix Table 3; states 'Small standard deviations signify that most of the gains from recursion are beyond the noise regime' - i.e. compares the gain to the seed band explicitly

title: The Effectiveness and Durability of Pretraining Data Filtering in Protein Language Models
claimed_delta: filtered vs unfiltered ESM-2: significant mutation-effect degradation only at 650M (-0.068, p=0.003) and 3B (-0.124, p=3e-4)
note: explicit and self-flagged: 'we limited our training runs above to a single seed per model, which reduces our confidence about the statistical significance of differences between models'. The fine-tuning follow-up uses 3 seeds and one of those three seeds is a visible outlier (0.244 vs 0.509 and 0.513 at step 500) - a concrete instance of the tail this project measures.

title: QProtFuse: Query-Guided Layer Fusion for Retrieval-Augmented Protein Function Prediction
note: All arms are ESM-2-derived and differ only in which layers are fused (query-guided vs fixed mean vs global weights). Layer choice within one PLM is neither a non-PLM representation nor a different PLM or scale, so I1 is not met. Judgment recorded because it is arguably a representation comparison in spirit; 3 seeds with mean+-SD if it is ever reconsidered.

title: HierDTA: Hierarchical Structure-Aware Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction
note: ESM-2 embeddings are a fixed component of every arm. The ablations are architectural (drug encoder type, No Augmentation, No Interaction, No TLA) and never swap the protein representation. Figure 4's comparison is 'generated from a single random seed'.

title: Generative Retrieval for Reverse Target Fishing with a Proteome-Scale Benchmark
note: ESMC-600M features are held fixed across GenFish and the adapted baselines by design; the claim is about generative vs discriminative retrieval, not about the representation, so I2 fails as well as I1. RELATED WORK, cite for practice: headline results use 5 seeds with paired molecule bootstrap, and the paper reports per-seed-pair outcomes ('GenFish leads in two of five seed pairs for R@10, three for R@50, and all five for MRR') and concludes the ordering is not statistically resolved. That is the n=1 gamble made visible by the authors themselves.

title: Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability
note: Arms are acceptance criteria (descriptive vs interventional) applied to ESM-2 and Pythia, scored through masked-residue predictions. No representation is compared against a baseline representation, and there is no trained head on a supervised task. The '5 seeds' are intervention seeds.

title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
note: The intervention is the training and retrieval corpus (clean vs poisoned), not the representation. No PLM-vs-baseline representation comparison.

title: ProtModernBERT: Compute-Efficient Protein Language Modeling
benchmarks: ProteinGym-style suite (organismal fitness, binding, expression, activity, stability)
claimed_delta: ProtModernBERT matches or beats ESM-2 and AMPLIFY at lower pretraining compute; highest organismal-fitness score
note: no seed, SD, error-bar or repetition language anywhere. The '8 different runs' are hyperparameter variants, not seeds. Also compares randomly initialised architectures, which is a representation comparison in its own right.

title: ProTok: Unified Protein Tokenization via Modular Multi-Codebook Quantization
claimed_delta: ProTok_str vs DPLM-2 and other tokenizers; e.g. BioLIP2 Cat.Fold AUROC 85.79 single run vs 88.37 best baseline
note: EXEMPLARY and directly comparable to Part B: Table S1 reruns the validation-selected configuration at five named seeds (1234, 42, 7, 2024, 31337) and prints the 5-seed mean+-SD beside the single-run value from Table 1. On BioLIP2 Cat.Fold the single run reads 85.79 against a 5-seed mean of 86.8+-0.2 - the headline number sits about 5 seed-SDs below its own mean, while the gap to the best baseline is 2.6. Exactly the failure mode this project measures, measured by the authors.

title: A System One Approach to General Protein Evolution
claimed_delta: Pev (frozen ESM-2 650M) vs ridge on one-hot site features and GP over the same features, plus zero-shot ESM-2 and random; 1.8x as many beneficial mutations as zero-shot ESM-2
note: no seed or repeated-run language anywhere; the standard deviations in the text are assay replicate SDs from the measurements, not run-to-run spread. The ridge comparator is refit in closed form and so is deterministic, but the Pev head is trained.

title: Linear Fitness Subspace in Protein Language Models Enables Sample-Efficient Directed Evolution
benchmarks: 10 core ProteinGym assays plus an extended set
claimed_delta: ridge on each representation: mutation one-hot 0.312, BLOSUM 0.451, conservation/MSA 0.535, mean-pooled PLM embedding 0.574, site-delta PLM feature 0.763
note: the cleanest I1(a) comparison in the pool so far - a single table pricing five representations under one surrogate. 5 random seeds for every supervised method, mean+-SD per assay, paired Wilcoxon across assays. The representation-ablation rows themselves carry no SD because the ridge fits are closed-form.

title: PIT-GCL: Protein Interaction using Topological Graph Contrastive Learning
claimed_delta: replacing the PLM sequence channel with one-hot identity costs a paired -0.0216 (p<1e-4); scaling the encoder four-fold costs -0.0037 (p=0.025)
note: EXEMPLARY and the closest match to this project's own prescription: the authors state that their margins are 'between 6.4 and 9.6 times the combined standard deviation of the two methods' - they compute the delta-over-seed-sd ratio themselves. They also say what a seed varies per benchmark (on PPIRef it redraws the whole 80/10/10 split, so the spread covers split, init and negative sampling). One wrinkle: the paired bootstrap is run on the seed-42 predictions only, while the arms ran at three seeds.

title: Learning Latent Protein Languages for Autoregressive Generation
claimed_delta: GCP-VQVAE Lite 2 vs FoldSeek, ProTokens, VanillaVQ, AIDO, ESM3, AminoAseed and GCP-VQVAE Large/Lite; functional AUROC 71.32 vs 72.43 best baseline, and +24.2% functional-site AUROC over the base tokenizer
note: the 'two runs' in the text are a training-speed comparison, not seeds. No seed repetition for the supervised probes.

title: Beyond Random Splits: Evaluating Drug-Target Affinity Models Under Chemically and Biologically Motivated Distribution Shifts
benchmarks: curated ChEMBL+BindingDB 718,800 pairs, four split regimes (scaffold, fingerprint-cluster, protein-cluster, dual OOD)
claimed_delta: Morgan-fingerprint + protein-CNN baseline (explicitly 'a non-pretrained protein encoder outside the ESM-2 design space') vs 12 ESM-2 architectures; mean validation RMSE 0.950/0.945 under chemical OOD rising to 1.299/1.321 under protein and dual OOD
note: the headline 66-architecture-pair rankings rest on one run each; only three representative architectures are repeated over three seeds, where the SD reaches 0.0358 RMSE under dual OOD. The paper's own claim is that split choice changes which architecture looks best - a ranking-stability claim built mostly on single runs.

title: Generative modeling of intrinsically disordered protein regions by reinforcing sparse autoencoder features
note: Arms are steering and RL strategies over one SAE feature space, scored by motif and compartment enrichment of generated IDRs. No representation is compared against a baseline representation on a supervised task. Three seeds with SDs, for generation metrics.

title: RipplePLM: Structural and Property Decoupling for Protein Mutation Effect Generation
benchmarks: low-N fitness regression on Spike-ACE2 and avGFP (MutaPLM protocol, 192 labels)
claimed_delta: Spike-ACE2 Spearman: Ridge Regression 0.335+-0.052, ESM-2 0.331+-0.041, Augmented ESM 0.363+-0.021, RipplePLM 0.491+-...; avGFP: Ridge 0.298+-0.071 vs ESM-2 0.554+-0.013
note: a real-world instance of the low-ratio regime from Part B: on Spike-ACE2 frozen ESM-2 (0.331+-0.041) sits BELOW a ridge baseline (0.335+-0.052), a gap of 0.004 against SDs of 0.04-0.05, so |delta|/sd is about 0.08. On avGFP the same pair differs by 0.256 with SDs of 0.013-0.071. Same two representations, two assays, opposite verdicts - and only the multi-run SDs make that readable.

title: Auditable Algebraic Counting Field for Cryptic-Pocket Detection from Apo Structures
claimed_delta: ACF (geometric/physicochemical/topological lookup tables) vs pLM-NN (the benchmark's ESM2-3B embedding plus trained head): mean paired ROC-AUC difference +0.0058 [-0.0168, +0.0276], p=0.598, ahead on 115 chains and behind on others
note: ACF's integer weights come from a closed-form ridge-regularized solve plus rounding, so that arm is deterministic, and the pLM baseline is a single released checkpoint. The 'seeds' in the text are data-halving and bootstrap seeds. The limitations section draws the exact distinction this project is built on: 'stability of individual weights across training splits and pairing seeds remain untested here; bootstrap-seed stability addresses a different question.' Note also that the headline representation contrast is reported as unresolved rather than as a win.

title: ORBIT-FMIB: Tracking Order-Resolved Epistatic Information Through ESM-2
note: Frozen ESM-2 representations are compared against a raw one-hot mutation encoding, but the one-hot arm is explicitly a control for estimator instability ('a sharp test of whether the observed instability lives in the estimator and training procedure'), not evidence about the representation, so I2 fails. RELATED WORK, cite with 2611.09046 (same programme): it retrains a 31-layer x 15-subset x 3-critic-seed grid (1,395 fits) from scratch and finds the two runs produced genuinely different critics, and reports a V100 and an H100 giving different scores for identical inputs. That last point is a hardware-level nondeterminism source this project's seed bands do not cover and the limitations should concede.

title: Analysis of Quantized and Efficiently Adapted Protein Language Models
claimed_delta: 4-bit quantization and QLoRA vs full fine-tuning across ESM-2 scales, ESMC and ProtBERT; reported as QLoRA/full score ratios, geometric means with 95% CIs over 3 seeds
note: triplicate across three seeds for every model-task cell, with SDs printed under each ratio. Touches GB1, so it is a candidate for the secondary outcome, though the arms are quantization and adapter choices across PLM families rather than a PLM-vs-non-PLM swap.

title: LEMON-ZEST: Evolution-Informed Tokenization for Efficient Protein Language Modeling
claimed_delta: ZEST tokenization vs character-level tokenization and a corpus-frequency BPE baseline, across three seeds and model scales (9 pretrained 50M+8M models with varying embedding tables)
note: the single most explicit statement of the conflation this project measures, in the authors' own limitations: 'the bootstrap intervals we report for our tokenizer comparison and ablations capture variability over evaluation queries, not variability across independent training runs. Due to limited compute, the full-scale models were trained with a single seed.' Quote this.

title: Drug-Target Interaction Prediction via Hierarchical Sequential Cross-Attention over Chemical and Protein Language Models
note: The chemical and protein language models are fixed in every arm; the ablation removes the CNN and the cross-attention module, and the other contrast is partial vs full fine-tuning. No representation swap. Worth quoting on practice: five runs were done during development but only the validation-selected checkpoint is reported, and the paper concedes 'a fully controlled benchmark with reimplemented baselines, identical splits, and reported mean and standard deviation across multiple seeds would provide a more rigorous empirical foundation'.
